CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Overview

nlmixr2plot is a pure-R package (no compiled code) that provides ‘ggplot2’ plotting methods for ‘nlmixr2’ objects: goodness-of-fit plots for fits, augPred() plots, trace plots, visual predictive checks (VPCs), and automatic compartment diagrams of ‘rxode2’/‘nlmixr2’ models. It depends on ‘rxode2’, ‘nlmixr2est’ and ‘nlmixr2extra’ for model handling and simulation; it has reverse dependencies (babelmixr2, nlmixr2, shinyMixR – see cran-comments.md).

Build and Development Commands

Install / Document

devtools::install()   # or from the shell: R CMD INSTALL .
devtools::document()  # regenerates man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen

NAMESPACE and man/*.Rd are generated by roxygen2 (markdown enabled); never edit them by hand.

Run Tests

NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test()"
# Single file: filter is the basename without "test-" and ".R"
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test(filter='model-diagram')"
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e "devtools::test(filter='vpc-data')"

Most test files fit real nlmixr2 models (with nlmixr2data data), so the full suite is slow. Many tests need Suggests packages (nlmixr2data, vpc, tidyvpc, DiagrammeR, dplyr, withr) and skip without them.

R CMD Check

devtools::check()   # or: R CMD build . && R CMD check nlmixr2plot_*.tar.gz

CI builds with --no-manual --compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf.

Lint and Format

air format .                              # air 0.11.0, settings in air.toml
Rscript -e "lintr::lint_package()"        # lintr 3.4.0, settings in .lintr

Run lintr from the package root (the .lintr test exclusions use list.files() relative to the working directory).

Architecture

All code lives in R/:

File Purpose
R/plot.nlmixr2.R plot.nlmixr2FitData() goodness-of-fit plots (DV/PRED/IPRED, residuals, per-endpoint via plotCmt()), .setupPlotData(), traceplot() generic and methods
R/plot.bsv.R Between-subject-variability plots (eta QQ, eta correlation, eta vs covariate) used by plot(fit, covariate = ...)
R/plot.nlmixr2AugPred.R plot.nlmixr2AugPred() (paginated individual plots, log = "x"/"y"/"xy")
R/vpcPlot.R vpcPlot(), vpcPlotTad(), vpcCens(), vpcCensTad() and the observed/simulated data setup helpers (.vpc*)
R/modelDiagram.R modelGraph(), modelDiagram(), plot.rxUi/plot.rxode2/plot.nlmixr2ModelGraph, print.nlmixr2ModelGraph; internals use the .md* prefix
R/reexports.R Re-exports geom_cens, geom_amt, stat_cens, stat_amt from rxode2
vignettes/model-diagrams.Rmd “Automatic model diagrams” vignette

Plot return values

Fit plots, BSV plots and augPred() plots return ggtibble::gglist objects (built with ggtibble::new_gglist() / as_gglist()), often named and nested. Keep that structure when adding plots; tests (test-gglist-integration.R) rely on it.

VPC backends

vpcPlot() has method = c("vpc", "tidyvpc"); when not supplied it uses ‘vpc’ if installed, otherwise ‘tidyvpc’. Both are Suggests, so guard any use with requireNamespace(). fit may also be a nlmixr2est::vpcSim() simulation. Observed data comes from the original (or supplied data) dataset; records with MDV = 1 or missing DV are dropped, and the matching simulated records must be dropped too so observed/simulated rows stay paired. Multiple-endpoint and censored VPCs stratify by endpoint and match simulated endpoint labels to the observed ones by name.

Model diagrams

modelGraph() parses the model’s d/dt() equations (the code says “parsed, not regex matched”) into a graph of nodes (compartments with a role such as dosing/central/effect) and edges (transfer, elimination, input, interaction), detecting dosing compartments from dosing records and showing lag()/f()/rate()/dur() as annotations. modelDiagram() lays it out (.mdLayout()) and draws it with one of three engines: "DiagrammeR" (default when installed), "ggplot2" (fallback) or "dot" (DOT source string). The default can be set with options(nlmixr2plot.diagram.engine = ...). DiagrammeR is a Suggests and must stay conditional. A fitted model keeps its goodness-of-fit plot(); plot() of an rxUi or compiled rxode2 model draws the diagram.

Testing Conventions

  • testthat edition 3; files are tests/testthat/test-*.R.
  • Tests run inside the package namespace: call internals by bare name; never use nlmixr2plot:::.
  • Guard optional dependencies with skip_if_not_installed(); guard fits that may fail with skip_if(inherits(fit, "try-error")).
  • Expensive tests must start with skip_on_cran().
  • tests/testthat.R partitions the suite for CI:
    • On CRAN/CI it forces single-threaded testing; on CRAN it also sets rxode2::setRxThreads(2L).
    • Push/PR CI (CI=true, NOT_CRAN=true) skips the slow files listed in .slow_batches (plots-multiple-endpoints, plots-cens, plots-bsv).
    • The weekly slow-tests.yaml workflow runs each batch via NLMIXR2PLOT_TEST_BATCH=<n>; the workflow’s batch matrix must match the number of entries in .slow_batches.
    • Locally and on CRAN everything runs. When a test file grows past a few minutes, move it into a batch.
  • tests/testthat/Rplots.pdf is a by-product of running tests; do not commit changes to it.

CI Workflows (.github/workflows/)

  • R-CMD-check.yaml – macOS, Windows, Ubuntu (devel, release, oldrel-1); installs the nlmixr2 stack (rxode2, nlmixr2est, nlmixr2extra, …) from GitHub.
  • slow-tests.yaml – weekly/manual slow test batches.
  • test-coverage.yaml, pkgdown.yaml – coverage and site (https://nlmixr2.github.io/nlmixr2plot/).
  • format-check.yaml – fails if air format would change files.
  • lint.yaml – lintr::lint_package() with lintr pinned at 3.4.0.

R Code Style

  • Exported functions: camelCase (vpcPlot, modelDiagram, plotCmt).
  • Internal functions and local variables: .camelCase with a leading dot (.setupPlotData, .vpcSimData, .mdLayout, .dat0, .lst).
  • S3 methods: generic.class (plot.nlmixr2FitData, traceplot.nlmixr2FitCore).
  • Use .data$col (imported from ggplot2) for tidy-eval column references in ggplot2 aesthetics.
  • Do not use ::: in package code or tests (CodeFactor flags it).
  • Use American English; ASCII only – no Unicode in R code, roxygen, tests, NEWS.md or this file (write --, ->, straight quotes).
  • Formatting is owned by air (line width 120, indent 2). air skips calls such as ini(), model(), rxode2() and quote() so rxode2 model syntax (d/dt(x), lcl <- 1; label("...")) is left as written.
  • lintr: line length 120; <<- allowed; infix_spaces_linter excludes /; object-name/usage linters are off. Test files are exempt from a set of style linters because they contain rxode2 model syntax.
  • Mechanical reformat commits go in .git-blame-ignore-revs (git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs).

Documentation and NEWS

  • Roxygen with markdown; examples that fit models are wrapped in \donttest{}. Code using a Suggests package in examples is guarded by requireNamespace().
  • Add a bullet to the top # nlmixr2plot (development version) section of NEWS.md for user-visible changes, referencing the issue ((#NN)).
  • README.md is generated from README.Rmd; edit the .Rmd.

Release / CRAN Cautions

  • Current CRAN release is 5.2.0 (CRAN-SUBMISSION); the dev version is 5.2.0.9000. Do not bump the version, edit cran-comments.md or CRAN-SUBMISSION unless asked.
  • Keep CRAN test/example/vignette time low: expensive work stays under skip_on_cran() or \donttest{}.
  • New files at the package root that are not part of the package must be added to .Rbuildignore.

CRAN tests: never assert on timing

  • Never put a wall-clock timing expectation in a test that can run on CRAN: no expect_lt()/expect_true() on Sys.time() differences, system.time(), proc.time(), bench/microbenchmark results, or any other elapsed-time threshold. CRAN check machines are shared and heavily loaded, so elapsed time there is random and a timing assertion fails at random. Example: nlmixr2plot test-model-diagram.R asserted a modelGraph() call took < 30 s; on CRAN it took 48.4 s and failed.
  • Test the result, not the speed. If a speed regression guard is really needed, put it only in a test that starts with skip_on_cran() (or the package’s own CRAN skip helper), and never in examples or vignettes.
  • Tests that take more than a few seconds should also skip on CRAN.
